label: Data-driven business questions
text: A marketing research analyst testing a new television advertisement; a pharmaceutical manufacturer comparing a new drug; an operations manager checking product quality; a software company reviewing call-centre satisfaction; management assessing 1st year MBA students in LMTSM.

label: Shark attacks and ice-cream sales
text: Both rise and fall together through the year because summer drives both: a spurious correlation.

label: Employee attrition rate
text: A statistician's model concluded that employees below the age of 30 who live 20+ miles from work do not stay long.

label: Retailer and HR examples
text: A retailer uses sales data to decide inventory stocking; HR managers use attrition statistics to plan hiring.

label: Quantitative techniques by function
text: Marketing: survey data to choose the most effective advertising channel. Finance: predicting stock price movements with time series analysis. Operations: route optimisation to minimise fuel costs. Human Resources: employee satisfaction survey data to improve retention.

label: Restaurant chain
text: A restaurant chain analyzes customer visit data to identify peak business hours and plan staffing.

label: Graph A (AIM) and Graph B (QTM)
text: Two class-performance curves: AIM peaks towards the right with a long left tail; QTM peaks towards the left with a long right tail.

label: Census and exit poll
text: Census is the example of descriptive statistics; exit poll is the example of inferential statistics.

label: Population and sample pairs
text: Songs from Bollywood movies (population) vs those that won the National Award (sample); participants of PGP in LMTSM vs those with less than 1 years of experience.

label: Florida Department of Tourism survey
text: Telephone survey of in-state residents; stratified by north, central and south Florida; random digit dialing; next-birthday method; sample size 868.

label: Sampling method examples
text: 200 of 2000 students (simple random); 25 of 500 students (systematic); India's N, S, W, E regions (stratified); a school's branches and TIET's departments (clustered).

label: CIGNA retirement services survey
text: Telephone survey by Gfk NOP World of 659 full-time employees over 18, 80 percent in a retirement plan; stratified by income and age.

label: Grouped classifications
text: Weight classes 40-45 to 95-100; marginal, small, medium and big farmers by hectares; revised MSME classification; education levels E0 to E5.

label: Runners and the four scales
text: Runner numbers (nominal), finishing places (ordinal), 0-to-10 performance ratings (interval), finishing time in seconds (ratio).

label: Customer details table
text: Customers A to G with salary, age, gender and family size, used to label record, data set, variable, discrete, continuous, qualitative and quantitative.

label: Survey questions classified
text: Facebook profile yes/no (categorical), text messages in three days (numerical discrete), app download time in seconds (numerical continuous).

label: Business decisions under uncertainty
text: Will a new product launch succeed? What is the likelihood a key client defaults on payment? How do supply chain disruptions affect fulfillment rates?

label: Examples of the three types of probability
text: Classical: dice, coins (all outcomes equally likely). Empirical: late deliveries out of the last 100. Subjective: a manager's estimate.

label: Shipping examples of probability terms
text: Experiment: rolling dice, shipping a product. Outcome: product arrives late. Event: shipment is delivered, or at least one defective item.

label: Drawing an ace from 52 cards
text: P(Ace) = 4/52 = 1/13 because a deck has 4 aces and 52 cards; P(Ace of Hearts) = 1/52.

label: Gaurav's odd and even gamble
text: Gaurav wins on odd numbers, the speaker wins on even numbers; {1, 3, 5} and {2, 4, 6} are both subsets of the sample space S.

label: Late deliveries, loan defaults and stockouts
text: 4 of 100 deliveries late: 4/100 = 0.04 or 4%. 3 of every 100 business loans default: 3/100 = 0.03 or 3%. 10 stockout days in 200 sales days: 10/200 = 0.05 or 5%.

label: Venn diagrams for A, B, complements, union and intersection
text: Six shaded Venn diagrams: A, B, A' (complement of A), B' (complement of B), A union B and A intersect B.

label: Shipments and a die roll as event types
text: Mutually exclusive: shipment arrives late and on time. Independent: two unrelated shipments. Mutually exhaustive: the events 1 to 6 on a single die roll.

label: Two good parts when 2% are defective
text: 2% of parts are defective, so each part is good with probability 0.98; both good: 0.98 x 0.98 = 0.9604 or 96.04%.

label: Warranty given a premium product
text: The probability a customer buys a warranty, given they purchased a premium product.

label: Choosing 1 of 20 midlevel managers
text: Age and gender data for 20 midlevel managers; P(woman or over 50) = 0.6 and P(under 30) = 0.1.

label: Machine out of control or down
text: P(out of control) = 0.02, P(down) = 0.015; the events are mutually exclusive; P(call a repair person) = 0.035; P(machine can produce) = 0.985, the complement of down.

label: IBM and AT&T projects
text: 100 projects: IBM 40 (30 computer, 10 telecommunications), AT&T 60 (40 telecommunications, 20 computer). Given telecommunications, P(IBM) = 10/50 = 0.2.

label: Consulting firm bidding for two jobs
text: P(job with firm A) = 0.45; if A is won, P(B also gives the job) = 0.90; chance of both jobs = 0.405.

label: Salary inequity check
text: Twenty-one per cent of executives at top salary, 40% are women, 6.4% are women at the top. 6.4% < 8.4%, so women are underrepresented at the top salary level.

label: Television and billboard ads
text: P(television commercial) = 0.04, P(billboard) = 0.06, independent. Both: 0.0024. At least one: 0.0976.

label: Defective wine corks
text: Cork defect rate 75%, four bottles opened, independent. All four defective: 0.316. At least one defective: 0.996.

label: Finding a qualifying consumer
text: 10% of the public uses the product; in a random sample of 10 people, P(at least 1 qualifies) = 0.6513.

label: Number of girls in four births
text: X = 0 to 4 girls; P(X) = 1/16, 4/16, 6/16, 4/16, 1/16 (0.0625, 0.2500, 0.3750, 0.2500, 0.0625), shown as a probability table and a bar chart.

label: Discrete money, continuous temperature
text: Discrete: money made on an investment, $500 or a loss of -$200, measured to the nearest cent. Continuous: temperature (36.111000099 degrees), weight, height, time.

label: Sum of two dice
text: Each of the 36 pairs has probability (1/6)(1/6) = 1/36. X = sum of dots, from 2 to 12, with P(2) = 1/36 rising to P(7) = 6/36 and back to P(12) = 1/36.

label: Telephone calls at an exchange
text: Calls per minute between noon and 1:00 P.M.: x = 0 to 5 with P(x) = 0.3, 0.2, 0.2, 0.1, 0.1, 0.1. Verify the distribution, find the cumulative distribution function, and find P(more than two calls) between 12:34 and 12:35 P.M.

label: Win or lose a dollar on a coin
text: Heads wins a dollar, tails loses a dollar; h(x) = 2X - 1; E[h(x)] = (-1)(.50) + (1)(.50) = 0.

label: Monthly sales and profit
text: Sales of 5,000 to 9,000 items with P(x) = 0.2, 0.3, 0.2, 0.2, 0.1; fixed monthly production cost $8,000; each item brings $2. Find expected monthly profit by the Type 1 and Type 2 formulas.

label: Variance of monthly profit
text: Profit = 2X - 8,000. E(X squared) = 46,500,000, E(X) = 6,700, V(X) = 1,610,000; variance of profit = 6,440,000; standard deviation = 2,537.72.

label: Oil well investment
text: Outcomes: -$40,000 (no oil) with .25, 10,000 (some oil) with .7, 70,000 (much oil) with .05. Find the expected monetary outcome and its variance.

label: Coin toss as a Bernoulli variable
text: Heads taken as 1 (success) and tails as 0 (failure): the outcome of a toss is a Bernoulli random variable.

label: Salad taken at a hotel
text: Amount of salad uniformly distributed between 5 ounces and 15 ounces; find the PD, expected value, variance, and P(between 12 and 15 ounces).

label: Where the normal distribution is used
text: Heights of people, scientific measurements, test scores, amounts of rainfall.

label: Toll plaza response time
text: Mean 160 microseconds, standard deviation 30. P(100 < X < 180) = P(-2 < Z < 0.6666) = 0.4772 + 0.2475 = 0.7247.

label: Semiconductor impurities
text: Mean 127 parts per million, standard deviation 22; acceptable below 150. P(X < 150) = P(Z < 1.045) = 0.5 + 0.3520 = 0.8520.

label: Where the CLT is used
text: Election polling, quality control, finance, and estimating average outcomes in populations.

label: Excel simulation article on the Central Limit Theorem
text: Additional reading: an American Journal of Business Education article on a Microsoft Excel simulation illustrating the Central Limit Theorem's appropriateness for comparing the difference between the means of any two populations.

label: Class Height Exercise
text: A class activity repeated through the deck: work out the population mean and sample mean, then the median, then the mode of the class's heights. No data is printed on the slides.

label: 2 Players' Problem
text: Runs scored by Player-1 and Player-2 in different matches, shown in two tables. The deck asks what you observe from the mean and median, and then from the mean, median and mode.

label: Median of 7 observations
text: 26, 18, 27, 12, 14, 27, 19 in ascending order is 12, 14, 18, 19, 26, 27, 27, so the median is the middle value, 19.

label: Median of 8 observations
text: 26, 18, 27, 12, 14, 27, 30, 19 in ascending order is 12, 14, 18, 19, 26, 27, 27, 30; the median is the average of the middle two values, (19 + 26)/2 = 22.5.

label: Annual income and property values
text: The median is the measure of location most often (not always) reported for annual income and property value data, because a few extremely large incomes or property values can inflate the mean.

label: Table 1-2 and its dot plot
text: A frequency table of data values from 18 to 56 with a dot plot marking the mode at 18, the median near 22 and the mean at 26.9.

label: Supplier-1 and Supplier-2
text: Supplier-1: 1,2,3,4,5,6,6,7,8,9,10,11. Supplier-2: 4,5,5,5,6,6,6,6,7,7,7,8. Both have Mean = Median = Mode = 6, but the first set is spread out and the second is clustered together.

label: CEO salary and the mean
text: If the CEO earns ₹10 crore and others average ₹6 lakh, the mean salary could mislead stakeholders.

label: Median home price
text: Median home price is often used by realtors because it is not inflated by a few luxury homes.

label: T-shirt sizes and menu combos
text: Fashion retail: the most sold t-shirt size (mode) guides inventory purchases. Restaurant menu: the mode meal ordered helps design new combos.

label: Three situations, three measures
text: Employees' salaries (skewed, most earn ₹40k but the CEO earns ₹8L): median. Best-selling product size (size M t-shirts): mode. Daily sales in a stable market (supermarket with consistent sales): mean.

label: Net worth of the 20 richest individuals
text: Forbes list for 2007: the net worth of the 20 richest individuals in billions of dollars (33, 26, 24, 21, 19, 20, 18, 18, 52, 56, 27, 22, 18, 49, 22, 20, 23, 32, 20, 18). Find the 50th and 80th percentiles.

label: 80th percentile of 70 values
text: For 70 values in ascending order, i = (80/100)70 = 56, so the 80th percentile is the average of the 56th and 57th values: (535 + 549)/2 = 542.

label: Stem-leaf plot
text: A stem-leaf plot with Count, Stem and Leaf columns, stems from 42 to 61; the first row is stem 42 with leaf 5 and the last row is stem 61 with leaves 5,5.

label: Monthly sales of 15 retail stores
text: Monthly sales (₹ lakhs) of 15 stores: 28, 34, 31, 41, 38, 27, 32, 36, 34, 30, 29, 44, 35, 39, 30. Tasks: stores below the average, the cluster of stores, four equal groups by quartile, and the top 10% for rewards.
